newsitem.title: UK: Major says "fair expectation" of May 1 UK election.
newsitem.headline: Major says "fair expectation" of May 1 UK election.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday there was a "fair expectation" that a British general election will be held on May 1.
"There is a fair expectation, but I think we will announce it in the normal constitutional way," Major said in reply to a question put to him during a BBC radio phone-in.
"The election is not going to be very far away, but there
is a lot of important legislation that is going through (parliament) at the moment," Major added.

Major was speaking on the day that Ben Chapman, the Labour victor of the Wirral South by-election which plunged his government into a minority in parliament, arrives to take his seat in the House of Commons.
Major denied having reached any understanding with the nine-strong Ulster Unionist Party to help him retain power.
"There are no deals with the Ulster Unionists," he said.
